title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's location data can be linked to the specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking of the child's movements across contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location with other attributes
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location type, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The Mobile App Backend processes identified location data of the child, which directly reveals the child's whereabouts.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's live location data can be linked to a specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking and association of location data with individual identity.
assumptions: Location data is associated with identifiable user accounts or devices

title: Profiling individual through location data
description: Live location data can be analyzed to profile a child's movements, routines, and patterns, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily activities and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data can be analyzed over time to derive behavioral patterns

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes identified personal data (child's live location) which directly reveals the identity and whereabouts of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data is inherently tied to specific individuals

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Live location data contains revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject, including real-time position, movement patterns, and proximity to sensitive locations.
assumptions: Location data alone or combined with other data can identify the child

title: Highly sensitive data type collected
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required. Real-time location tracking exceeds typical privacy expectations for children.
assumptions: Live location is considered sensitive data under privacy regulations

title: Excessive data granularity
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level (real-time, continuous tracking) which is more granular than typically needed for guardian access purposes.
assumptions: Guardians may not need real-time continuous location updates

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated from the backend to an external entity (secondary guardian) where it may be accessible beyond the intended scope of the application.
assumptions: External entities may have different security controls than the backend

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Location data is made accessible to a predetermined set of parties (secondary guardians) which may exceed functional necessity if guardianship access is not strictly required.
assumptions: Not all children require secondary guardian access to location data

title: Child unaware of location sharing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Children may not understand the implications of location sharing

title: Lack of control over location sharing preferences
description: The child or parent may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how, when, and with whom location data is shared.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be insufficient or not available

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing live location data may violate data minimization principles if the data collected exceeds what is functionally necessary for the stated purpose of guardian access.
assumptions: GDPR and similar regulations require data minimization

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Location data collection and sharing may not rely on valid consent, especially if consent is not properly obtained from the child or legal guardian.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be inadequate for children's data

title: Data Propagation to External Analytics Partner
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics are propagated from the backend to an external advertising/analytics partner (EE4) beyond what may be strictly necessary for the app's free tier functionality.
assumptions: The analytics partner may use this data for purposes beyond funding the free tier, or the data may be further shared with third parties.

title: Predetermined External Data Recipient
description: Personal data is shared with a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) that may not be functionally necessary for the core app functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known third party that may have its own data processing policies.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement analytics are being shared with external advertising/analytics partners to fund the free tier.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate this data sharing practice, or users may not read/understand them.

title: Lack of User Control Over Data Sharing
description: Users may lack control to opt-out of analytics data sharing with the advertising partner, or to customize which data is shared.
assumptions: The app may not provide granular consent options for this specific data flow.

title: Violation of Data Minimization Principle
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may include more personal data than strictly necessary to fund the app's free tier, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The analytics data may contain more granular information than needed for the stated purpose.

title: Potential Invalid Consent for Data Sharing
description: The data sharing with the advertising partner may rely on consent that is not valid (e.g., not freely given, not specific, or not informed).
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not adequately address this specific data flow.

title: Quasi-Identifier Re-identification Risk
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device IDs, usage patterns, timestamps) that could be combined with other data to re-identify individuals.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficiently robust to prevent re-identification when combined with external data sources.
uncertainty_note: Assumes aggregation is not truly anonymized and could be reverse-engineered.

title: Quasi-identifiers in Analytics Data
description: The analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., usage frequency, session duration, feature usage) that serve as quasi-identifiers and could identify specific users.
assumptions: Aggregated data may still retain enough detail to identify individuals in small user populations.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual granularity and aggregation methods used.
